stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• K2 is the second-highest mountain in the world, at 8,611 metres.
• It lies in the Karakoram range, on the border between Pakistan and China.
• It was first climbed in 1954 by an Italian expedition.
• Climbers call it the "Savage Mountain" because it is so difficult and dangerous.

The student wants to emphasize where K2 is located. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: K2 stands in the Karakoram range, on the Pakistan–China border.
An Italian expedition made the first ascent of K2 in 1954.
K2, known as the "Savage Mountain," is famously hard to climb.
At 8,611 metres, K2 is the second-highest mountain in the world.
explanation: Only this choice gives K2's location: its range and the border it sits on. The other choices are accurate but describe its height, its reputation or its first ascent instead.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Shalimar Gardens in Lahore were built in the 1640s during the reign of Shah Jahan.
• The gardens are laid out in three terraces, each lower than the one before.
• They contain more than 400 fountains.
• In 1981 they were named a UNESCO World Heritage Site together with the Lahore Fort.

The student wants to describe the layout of the Shalimar Gardens. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In 1981, UNESCO listed the Shalimar Gardens and the Lahore Fort as a World Heritage Site.
The Shalimar Gardens date from the reign of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.
The Shalimar Gardens are arranged in three terraces that step down one after another.
Built in the 1640s under Shah Jahan, the Shalimar Gardens are one of Lahore's best-known sights.
explanation: The terraces describe how the gardens are laid out, which is the goal. The choices about the 1640s, Shah Jahan or UNESCO give history, not layout.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2022, researcher Nida Qureshi studied the effect of lighting in classrooms.
• She compared 40 classrooms with large windows to 40 classrooms with small windows.
• Students in rooms with large windows scored 9 percent higher on reading tests, on average.
• Qureshi suggested that natural light may improve concentration.

The student wants to present the main finding of Qureshi's study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Qureshi found that students in classrooms with large windows scored about 9 percent higher on reading tests.
In 2022, the researcher Nida Qureshi studied how lighting affects students in classrooms.
Qureshi's 2022 study compared forty classrooms that had large windows with forty classrooms whose windows were small.
According to Qureshi, natural light may help students concentrate.
explanation: The finding is the 9 percent difference in reading scores, and only this choice states it. The choice about forty classrooms of each kind describes the method, and the choice about concentration gives Qureshi's suggested explanation rather than what she found.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The cheetah and the pronghorn are both among the fastest land animals.
• The cheetah lives mainly in Africa; the pronghorn lives in North America.
• The cheetah can sprint at about 100 kilometres per hour, but only for short bursts.
• The pronghorn can keep up a speed of about 55 kilometres per hour over several kilometres.

The student wants to contrast the running abilities of the two animals. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The cheetah can reach about 100 kilometres per hour, though only in short bursts.
The cheetah sprints at about 100 km per hour in short bursts, while the pronghorn holds about 55 km per hour for kilometres.
Both the cheetah and the pronghorn rank among the fastest land animals on Earth.
The cheetah lives mainly in Africa, whereas the pronghorn, another very fast animal, is found in North America.
explanation: Only this choice sets the cheetah's short sprints against the pronghorn's long-distance speed. The choice about Africa and North America is a contrast, but of where the animals live, not how they run.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Truck art is a style of decoration found on trucks and buses in Pakistan.
• Artists cover vehicles with bright flowers, birds, landscapes and lines of poetry.
• A fully decorated truck can cost its owner several months' income.
• Truck art has been shown in galleries abroad.

The student wants to introduce truck art to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The owner of a truck decorated in this style may spend several months' income on a single vehicle's paintwork.
Artists who paint trucks often add landscapes and lines of poetry.
Truck art has been shown in galleries outside Pakistan.
Truck art, a Pakistani style of vehicle decoration, covers trucks and buses with flowers, birds and poetry.
explanation: An unfamiliar audience needs to know what truck art is and what it looks like, which this choice explains. The other choices assume the reader already knows what "truck art" or "this style" refers to.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Ecologist Farhan Malik studies the Indus river dolphin, which is found mainly in Pakistan.
• The dolphin is nearly blind and finds food by echolocation.
• Malik's project aims to learn how irrigation barrages affect where the dolphins can travel.
• He has placed underwater sound recorders along a 200-kilometre stretch of the river.

The student wants to emphasize the aim of Malik's research. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Malik has placed underwater sound recorders along a 200-kilometre stretch of the Indus River.
The Indus river dolphin, which is nearly blind, finds its food by echolocation.
Farhan Malik is an ecologist who studies the Indus river dolphin, found mainly in Pakistan.
Malik wants to find out how irrigation barrages affect where Indus river dolphins can travel.
explanation: The aim is what the project wants to learn: how barrages affect the dolphins' movement. The choice about sound recorders describes Malik's method, not his aim.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Many traditional buildings in hot, dry regions have thick walls of mud or stone.
• Thick walls absorb heat during the day and release it slowly at night.
• Traditional houses in Yazd, Iran, also use tall wind-catching towers to cool their rooms.
• Old havelis in Lahore are built around shaded inner courtyards.

The student wants to make a generalization about traditional buildings in hot, dry regions. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Both Yazd's houses and Lahore's havelis are examples of traditional buildings.
In hot, dry regions, traditional buildings often have thick walls that absorb heat by day and release it at night.
In the Iranian city of Yazd, traditional houses have tall towers that catch passing winds and channel them into the rooms.
Old havelis in Lahore are arranged around inner courtyards that give shade.
explanation: A generalization covers buildings across the region, as this choice does. The choices about Yazd and Lahore describe particular places, so they are specific examples rather than general statements.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Indus Science Fair is an annual competition for secondary school students.
• The first fair was held in Sukkur in 2016.
• Students present projects on water, energy and farming.
• Winners receive scholarships funded by local businesses.
• The 2024 fair attracted more than 1,200 entrants.

The student wants to state when and where the first Indus Science Fair took place. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Winners at the annual Indus Science Fair receive scholarships from local businesses.
More than 1,200 students entered the Indus Science Fair in 2024.
At the Indus Science Fair, students present projects on water, energy and farming.
The first Indus Science Fair was held in Sukkur in 2016.
explanation: Only this choice gives both the place, Sukkur, and the year, 2016, of the first fair. The choice about 2024 gives a date, but for a later fair and without a place.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Mehwish and her brother Omar both run small bakeries in Multan.
• Mehwish sells mostly through a phone app that delivers to people's homes.
• Omar sells only from the counter of his shop.
• Both bakeries are known for their nan khatai biscuits.

The student wants to emphasize a difference between how Mehwish and Omar sell their goods. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The bakeries run by Mehwish and Omar are both known for their nan khatai biscuits.
Mehwish and Omar, who are brother and sister, both run small bakeries in Multan.
Mehwish sells most of her baked goods through a phone app that delivers them to people's homes.
Mehwish sells mostly through a home-delivery app, while Omar sells only from his shop counter.
explanation: This choice sets the two selling methods side by side. The choice about the phone app describes only Mehwish, so it shows no difference, and the other two choices stress what the siblings share.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• An urban heat island is a city area that is noticeably warmer than the surrounding countryside.
• Concrete and asphalt absorb sunlight during the day and release the heat slowly.
• A 2021 study found that central Karachi was up to 4 °C warmer at night than nearby rural land.
• Planting trees and using light-coloured roofs can reduce the effect.

The student wants to explain to an audience unfamiliar with the term what an urban heat island is and one cause of it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: According to a 2021 study, central Karachi was up to 4 °C warmer at night than the rural land around it.
Concrete and asphalt absorb sunlight during the day and then release the heat slowly.
An urban heat island, a city area warmer than the nearby countryside, forms partly because concrete and asphalt store heat.
Planting trees and using light-coloured roofs can reduce the urban heat island effect in cities such as Karachi.
explanation: The goal has two parts, a definition and a cause, and only this choice gives both. The choice about concrete and asphalt names the cause but never says what an urban heat island is.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Many rural schools in Thar lack reliable electricity.
• Without power, their computer labs and fans cannot be used.
• A pilot project installed solar panels on the roofs of 25 of these schools.
• Attendance at those schools rose by 12 percent during the hot months.

The student wants to present the result of the pilot project. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: After solar panels were put on 25 schools in Thar, their attendance in the hot months rose by 12 percent.
Rural schools in Thar often lack the reliable electricity needed for computer labs.
Many rural schools in Thar cannot use their computer labs or fans, because they lack reliable electricity.
A pilot project installed solar panels on the roofs of 25 rural schools in Thar.
explanation: The result is the 12 percent rise in attendance, which only this choice reports. The choice about installing panels describes what the project did, not what came of it.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Ibn al-Haytham was an 11th-century scholar who studied light and vision.
• He tested his ideas with careful experiments.
• Galileo Galilei was a 17th-century scientist who studied motion and astronomy.
• He also tested his ideas with experiments.

The student wants to emphasize a similarity between Ibn al-Haytham and Galileo. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Galileo, a 17th-century scientist, studied motion as well as the planets and stars.
Ibn al-Haytham studied light and vision, while Galileo studied motion and astronomy.
Both Ibn al-Haytham and Galileo tested their ideas through experiments.
Ibn al-Haytham lived in the 11th century, about six centuries before Galileo.
explanation: Testing ideas by experiment is what the two men shared. The choice about their subjects contrasts them, and the choice about centuries stresses the gap between them.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Tarbela Dam on the Indus River was completed in 1976.
• It is one of the largest earth-filled dams in the world.
• Its reservoir stores water for irrigation across Punjab and Sindh.
• Its power station generates electricity for the national grid.

The student wants to emphasize the size of the Tarbela Dam. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The Tarbela Dam's power station supplies electricity to the national grid.
Tarbela, on the Indus River, is one of the largest earth-filled dams in the world.
Completed in 1976, the Tarbela Dam stands on the Indus River.
Water stored behind the Tarbela Dam irrigates farmland across both Punjab and Sindh.
explanation: Calling Tarbela one of the largest earth-filled dams in the world stresses its size. The choice about irrigation across two provinces tells what the dam does, not how big it is.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Researchers long believed that a hawkmoth species in northern Pakistan fed only at night.
• In 2023, a team led by Sana Iqbal filmed the moths feeding at midday on alpine flowers.
• Those flowers open only in daylight.
• Iqbal argues that the moths may be important daytime pollinators.

The student wants to emphasize how Iqbal's findings challenge an earlier belief. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The alpine flowers on which the hawkmoths were filmed open only during the day.
In 2023, Sana Iqbal's team filmed hawkmoths in northern Pakistan feeding on alpine flowers.
Although the moths were long thought to feed only at night, Iqbal's team filmed them feeding at midday.
Iqbal argues that the hawkmoths may be important pollinators of flowers that open only in daylight.
explanation: Only this choice states the earlier belief and the finding that contradicts it. The others report Iqbal's work without mentioning the belief it challenges.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Sea of Green is a 2019 novel by the writer Rabia Hasan.
• It follows a young tea picker in the hills of Sri Lanka.
• It has been translated into eleven languages.
• Hasan grew up on a tea estate herself.

The student wants to introduce the novel Sea of Green and its author. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Rabia Hasan, who grew up on a tea estate herself, has seen her work translated into eleven languages.
Translated into eleven languages, the novel follows a young tea picker in Sri Lanka.
Sea of Green, a 2019 novel by Rabia Hasan, follows a young tea picker in Sri Lanka's hills.
Rabia Hasan's novel has been translated into eleven languages.
explanation: This choice names the novel, its author and what it is about. The others leave out the title or the author, so they do not introduce both.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Bioplastics are plastics made from plant materials such as corn starch or sugarcane.
• Ordinary plastics are made from oil.
• Some bioplastics break down within a few months in industrial composting facilities.
• Bioplastics currently cost more to produce than ordinary plastics.

The student wants to emphasize an advantage of some bioplastics over ordinary plastics. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Corn starch and sugarcane are among the materials used to make bioplastics.
Unlike ordinary plastics, some bioplastics break down within months in industrial composting facilities.
Bioplastics are made from plant materials such as corn starch or sugarcane.
Bioplastics currently cost more to produce than ordinary plastics, which are made from oil.
explanation: Breaking down quickly is an advantage, and this choice compares it directly with ordinary plastics. The choice about cost points to a disadvantage, and the choices about corn starch and sugarcane only describe what bioplastics are made of.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2021, agronomist Imran Butt studied wheat farms in southern Punjab.
• He divided 60 farms into two groups.
• Farms in one group had their fields levelled by laser; the others did not.
• Farms with laser-levelled fields used 25 percent less irrigation water.
• Wheat yields were similar in both groups.

The student wants to describe the method Butt used in his study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Butt divided 60 farms into two groups, only one of which had its fields levelled by laser.
In 2021, agronomist Imran Butt carried out a study of wheat farms in southern Punjab.
Butt found that farms with laser-levelled fields used 25 percent less water but produced similar yields.
Laser land levelling cut water use by a quarter on the farms Butt studied, without lowering wheat yields.
explanation: A method is how the study was set up, which this choice explains: two groups, one with laser-levelled fields. The choices about water use and yields give results, and the choice about 2021 gives only the time and place.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Engineer Kamran Aziz designed a low-cost incubator for newborn babies.
• It can run on a car battery when the mains power fails.
• It costs about one-tenth as much as a standard hospital incubator.
• Aziz's goal was to help small clinics that cannot afford standard incubators or lack a steady power supply.
• It has been tested in clinics in Sindh and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

The student wants to explain the purpose of Aziz's design. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Clinics in Sindh and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have tested the low-cost incubator that Aziz designed.
Aziz's incubator, which can keep running on a car battery when the mains power fails, costs about one-tenth as much as a standard model.
Engineer Kamran Aziz has designed an incubator for newborn babies.
Aziz designed his incubator to help small clinics that cannot afford standard incubators or lack steady power.
explanation: The purpose is the problem Aziz meant to solve, which only this choice states. The choice about the car battery and the price lists features of the design, not the reason for it.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Lahore Museum was founded in 1865.
• Its present building on The Mall opened in 1894.
• It holds a large collection of Gandhara art.
• John Lockwood Kipling, father of the writer Rudyard Kipling, was one of its early curators.

The student wants to emphasize when the museum's present building opened. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The Lahore Museum's present building on The Mall opened in 1894.
John Lockwood Kipling was one of the Lahore Museum's early curators.
The Lahore Museum, which holds a large Gandhara collection, stands on The Mall.
Founded in 1865, the Lahore Museum is known for its Gandhara art.
explanation: Only this choice gives the opening date of the present building, 1894. The choice with 1865 is tempting, but that is when the museum was founded, not when its present building opened.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A 2023 survey asked 2,000 university students in Pakistan where they mainly get their news.
• 64 percent said social media.
• 21 percent said television.
• 9 percent said newspapers or news websites.
• The rest gave other answers.

The student wants to emphasize how far ahead social media was of the next most common news source. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Only 9 percent of the students surveyed relied mainly on newspapers or news websites.
Social media, chosen by 64 percent of students, was used about three times as often as television, the next choice at 21 percent.
The 2023 survey found that 64 percent of 2,000 university students in Pakistan relied mainly on social media for their news.
Television, the main source for 21 percent of students, came second.
explanation: To show how far ahead social media was, it must be compared with the runner-up, television, as this choice does. The choice giving 64 percent of 2,000 students reports social media's share without any comparison.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Karakoram Highway links Pakistan with China.
• It is about 1,300 kilometres long.
• It passes through the Hunza valley.
• At the Khunjerab Pass it reaches a height of about 4,700 metres.

The student wants to emphasize how high the Karakoram Highway climbs. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: On its way to China, the Karakoram Highway passes through the Hunza valley.
The Karakoram Highway connects Pakistan and China across the mountains.
At the Khunjerab Pass, the Karakoram Highway climbs to about 4,700 metres.
The Karakoram Highway, about 1,300 kilometres long, links Pakistan with China.
explanation: Height is the goal, and only this choice gives the road's highest point. The choice with 1,300 kilometres is tempting because it gives a large figure, but that figure is length, not height.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Chemist Amna Siddiqui developed a paper strip that tests drinking water for arsenic.
• The strip changes colour within ten minutes if arsenic levels are unsafe.
• Each strip costs less than Rs 20.
• Laboratory tests for arsenic can take several days and cost thousands of rupees.

The student wants to compare Siddiqui's strip with laboratory tests in terms of speed and cost. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Laboratory tests for arsenic in drinking water can take several days and cost thousands of rupees.
Each of the arsenic-testing strips developed by the chemist Amna Siddiqui costs less than Rs 20.
Siddiqui's strip gives a result in ten minutes for under Rs 20, whereas laboratory tests can take days and cost thousands of rupees.
Amna Siddiqui's paper strip changes colour within ten minutes if a water sample contains unsafe levels of arsenic.
explanation: A comparison needs both the strip and the laboratory test, on both speed and cost, and only this choice gives all four facts. Each other choice describes only one side.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Crop rotation is the practice of growing different crops on the same land in successive seasons.
• Legumes such as lentils and chickpeas add nitrogen to the soil.
• Many farmers in Punjab grow wheat in winter and cotton or rice in summer.
• Rotation can also break the life cycles of pests.

The student wants to explain how crop rotation can benefit the soil. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Rotating crops from one season to the next can also help farmers by breaking the life cycles of the pests that attack their fields.
Crop rotation means growing different crops on the same land in successive seasons.
Many farmers in Punjab grow wheat in winter and cotton or rice in summer.
Including legumes such as lentils or chickpeas in a rotation enriches the soil, because these crops add nitrogen to it.
explanation: Only this choice links rotation to a benefit for the soil: legumes add nitrogen. Breaking pest life cycles is a real benefit, but it is not a benefit to the soil.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A 2018 study in Islamabad found that children who read for pleasure scored higher on vocabulary tests.
• The Islamabad study surveyed 600 children aged 8–11.
• A 2020 study in Dhaka found the same link among teenagers.
• The Dhaka study surveyed 900 teenagers aged 13–16.

The student wants to emphasize that the two studies reached a similar conclusion despite studying different age groups. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Though one studied children aged 8–11 and the other teenagers aged 13–16, both studies linked reading for pleasure with stronger vocabulary.
The Islamabad study surveyed 600 children aged 8–11, while the Dhaka study surveyed 900 teenagers aged 13–16.
A 2018 study in Islamabad found that children who read for pleasure scored higher on vocabulary tests.
Both the Islamabad study and the Dhaka study surveyed hundreds of young people about their reading.
explanation: The goal has two parts, the shared conclusion and the different age groups, and only this choice gives both. The choice comparing 600 children with 900 teenagers shows the difference but not the shared finding.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The markhor is a wild goat found in the mountains of northern Pakistan.
• It is Pakistan's national animal.
• Males have long, corkscrew-shaped horns.
• It feeds on grasses in summer and on leaves and twigs in winter.

The student wants to describe the markhor's diet. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The markhor lives in the mountains of northern Pakistan.
Male markhor have long horns shaped like corkscrews.
The markhor eats grasses in summer and leaves and twigs in winter.
Pakistan's national animal, the markhor, is a wild goat of the northern mountains.
explanation: A diet is what an animal eats, which only this choice describes. The other choices give the markhor's status, appearance and habitat.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 1990, a village in Swat had one primary school, which only boys attended.
• Today the village has four schools, two of them for girls.
• Literacy among women in the village has risen from about 10 percent to about 55 percent.
• Most of the new schools were built by a community trust.

The student wants to emphasize how much women's literacy in the village has changed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In 1990, this village in Swat had only a single primary school, which was attended only by boys.
The village now has four schools, two of which are for girls.
Literacy among the village's women has risen from about 10 percent to about 55 percent.
Most of the village's new schools were built by a community trust.
explanation: Only this choice gives the before-and-after literacy figures for women. The choice about four schools shows a change in schooling, but it says nothing about literacy.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A qanat is an underground channel that carries water from an aquifer to fields or villages.
• Qanats slope gently downhill, so water flows through them by gravity without pumps.
• Vertical shafts along the route let workers dig and clean the channel.
• In Balochistan, where they are called karez, qanats are still in use.

The student wants to explain how a qanat moves water without pumps. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Vertical shafts along a qanat's route allow workers to dig and clean the underground channel.
Known in Balochistan as karez, qanats are still in use in parts of that province.
A qanat is an underground channel that brings water from an aquifer to fields.
Because a qanat slopes gently downhill, water flows through it by gravity alone.
explanation: The gentle slope and gravity explain the movement of water, which is the goal. The choice about vertical shafts explains how a qanat is built and maintained, not how water moves through it.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Sleep researchers have long known that sleep helps people remember facts.
• In 2022, Hamza Rauf tested whether sleep also helps people learn physical skills.
• Participants practised a piano melody and then either slept or stayed awake for eight hours.
• Those who slept then played the melody with 20 percent fewer errors.

The student wants to present Rauf's findings to an audience already familiar with the link between sleep and memory for facts. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Rauf's 2022 study, participants practised a piano melody and then either slept or stayed awake for eight hours before playing it again.
Rauf found that sleep may help with physical skills too: people who slept after practising a melody made 20 percent fewer errors.
In 2022, Hamza Rauf studied whether sleep helps people learn physical skills.
Sleep researchers have long known that a night's sleep helps people remember facts.
explanation: This audience already knows about sleep and facts, so the useful new point is Rauf's result about physical skills, which this choice gives. The choice about facts repeats what the audience knows, and the other two give Rauf's question and method but not his findings.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Badshahi Mosque in Lahore was built under the emperor Aurangzeb.
• It was completed in 1673.
• Its courtyard can hold about 100,000 worshippers.
• It is built of red sandstone decorated with marble.

The student wants to emphasize the capacity of the Badshahi Mosque. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Completed in 1673, the Badshahi Mosque was built under the emperor Aurangzeb.
The courtyard of Lahore's Badshahi Mosque can hold about 100,000 worshippers.
The Badshahi Mosque is made of red sandstone decorated with marble.
The emperor Aurangzeb ordered the building of the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore.
explanation: Capacity means how many people a place can hold, which only this choice states. The other choices give the mosque's history and materials.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A city council is considering two ways to reduce traffic in its old quarter.
• Plan A would close the main street to cars at weekends.
• Plan B would charge drivers Rs 200 to enter the old quarter on weekdays.
• Plan A would cost little to put in place.
• Plan B would raise money that could be spent on buses.

The student wants to emphasize an advantage of Plan B. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Plan A, which would close the main street to cars at weekends, would cost very little to put in place.
Plan B, a Rs 200 weekday entry charge, would raise money that could be spent on buses.
Under Plan B, drivers would pay Rs 200 to enter the old quarter on weekdays.
The council is weighing two plans for reducing traffic in the city's old quarter.
explanation: Raising money for buses is an advantage of Plan B, and this choice states it. The choice about low cost gives an advantage, but of Plan A, and the choice about Rs 200 describes Plan B without saying what is good about it.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Novelist Usman Ghani writes long, slow-moving novels with many characters.
• Short-story writer Farah Naz writes brief, fast-paced stories with one or two characters.
• Both writers set their work in Karachi.
• Ghani writes in Urdu; Naz writes in English.

The student wants to emphasize a difference in the length and pace of the two writers' work. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Ghani's novels are long and slow-moving, whereas Naz's stories are brief and fast-paced.
Although both set their work in Karachi, Ghani writes his fiction in Urdu, while Naz writes hers in English.
Both Usman Ghani and Farah Naz set their fiction in the city of Karachi.
Usman Ghani writes long, slow-moving novels that feature many characters.
explanation: Only this choice contrasts the two writers on length and pace. The choice about Urdu and English is a difference too, but of language, and the choice about Ghani describes only one writer.

stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Some plants protect themselves by forming partnerships with ants.
• The bullhorn acacia of Central America gives ants shelter in its hollow thorns and food in the form of sugary nectar.
• In return, the ants attack insects and animals that try to eat the tree's leaves.
• The ants also cut away vines that grow on the tree.

The student wants to present the bullhorn acacia as an example that illustrates a general point. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The bullhorn acacia gives ants shelter in its hollow thorns and food in the form of sugary nectar.
The ants that live on the bullhorn acacia cut away vines that grow on the tree.
Some plants protect themselves by forming partnerships with ants.
Some plants rely on ants for protection; for example, the bullhorn acacia feeds and shelters ants that attack its leaf-eaters.
explanation: Only this choice states the general point and then presents the acacia as an example of it. The choice about the general point alone gives no example, and the other two describe the acacia without connecting it to any wider claim.

Saleem created Rasta after her father began using a wheelchair.
Rasta, an app made by Hira Saleem in 2021, now lists more than 3,000 places.

Unlike most spiders, the diving bell spider lives underwater, in an air bubble that it holds in place with silk.
The diving bell spider, like most other spiders, makes silk.
Most spiders, including many of the species found in Europe and Asia, use the webs they spin to catch their prey.

Because the trial did not measure protection beyond one year, the researchers are planning a longer follow-up study.
The researchers who tested a new malaria vaccine on 1,500 children are planning a follow-up study.
In a 2024 trial involving 1,500 children in two districts, a new malaria vaccine reduced cases by 60 percent over one year.
explanation: Only this choice gives both the result and the limitation. The choice with 1,500 children reports the result without any limitation, and the choice about the follow-up study gives the limitation without the result.

Ajrak is usually dyed in deep red and indigo blue.

In 2010, floods covered about one-fifth of Pakistan's land area.

Formal Hindi takes much of its vocabulary from Sanskrit.

The student wants to emphasize the most surprising finding of the study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Most of the noise in the market lanes came from loudspeakers and generators.
Busy main roads in Lahore averaged 78 decibels, compared with 62 decibels for residential lanes.
Some narrow market lanes, at an average of 81 decibels, were even louder than Lahore's busy main roads.
The researchers measured noise in 50 streets in Lahore, from main roads to residential lanes.
explanation: One would expect main roads to be the loudest, so narrow lanes being louder is the surprise, and this choice presents it. The choice comparing main roads with residential lanes gives an expected result.

The Rosetta Stone carries the same text in three different scripts, one of them ancient Greek.
Found in Egypt in 1799, the Rosetta Stone carries one text written in three scripts: hieroglyphic, Demotic and ancient Greek.
Because the stone repeats one text in Greek, which scholars could read, it helped Champollion decipher hieroglyphs.
explanation: The stone mattered because a readable Greek version unlocked the same text in hieroglyphs, and only this choice explains that link. The choice about three scripts describes the stone but does not say why scholars being able to read Greek made it useful.

• A 2023 study measured a yearly average of 85 micrograms per cubic metre in an industrial city.
• A nearby hill town measured 22 micrograms per cubic metre.

The student wants to emphasize how far both places exceeded the WHO guideline. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: A 2023 study found a yearly PM2.5 average of 85 micrograms per cubic metre in an industrial city.
Both places exceeded the WHO guideline of 5 micrograms: the hill town by more than four times, the industrial city by seventeen times.
The WHO recommends that yearly PM2.5 levels average no more than 5 micrograms per cubic metre.
The industrial city's yearly average of 85 micrograms was nearly four times the hill town's 22 micrograms.
explanation: Comparing each place with the guideline gives 22 ÷ 5 = 4.4 and 85 ÷ 5 = 17, as this choice states. The choice comparing 85 with 22 is accurate but compares the two places with each other, not with the WHO guideline.
